Patch Set 5:

(8 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Mostly good, comments inline. No correctness problems found: the pccs_attaches_queued increment/decrement pairs are balanced on every path (kthread_create() failure goes through pcc_attach_context_free() at the out: label, success frees in pcc_readonly_attach_thread()), and the atomic_dec() runs before fput(pccx->pccx_file) so the superblock is still pinned by the file's mount reference. The comments are mostly about naming, an untunable knob and commit-message completeness. As the message itself notes, there is no test: sanity-pcc.sh already drives pcc_async_threshold, so a case that lowers the queue depth and checks that attaches fall back to sync would fit naturally there once the parameter is settable.

commit.subject: LU-10499 pcc: Limit attach queue depth
commit.message:
LU-10499 pcc: Limit attach queue depth

The existing async attach code does not attempt to limit
the number of async attaches that can be requested at once.
This is a problem because we could theoretically create too
many kthreads and overwhelm the system.

When the attach queue depth is exceeded, we stop allowing
new items to be queued by switching over to sync attach.

Ideally we would rebuild the attach code to generate a
queue of attach requests and have the attach thread code
pull items from the queue until it's exhausted, but that's
a much more substantial change and is left for later.

It's really hard to remember what 'inode' and 'file' mean
when there's more than one in a function, so I've redone
some of the names here.

EX-6399 pcc: add tunable parameter for PCC attach thread

Add a tunable parameter llite.*.pcc_attach_thread_max to
tune the max number of kernel threads doing asynchronous
attach (1024 by default).

Was-Change-Id: Ic59c15af935dd8dff586fa6be3939d4322c136d5

Use variable names that are consistent with parameter name.
Add llite.pcc_attach_thread_max.4 man page for parameter.

Fixes: 5be466e87304 ("LU-10499 pcc: async attach in the background for PCC-RO file")
